# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

I see the bomb clearly: a display showing "0", an orange light, and three wires colored red, yellow, and blue. I am Deaf, so I cannot hear any speech from Mute or Blind, but I can see their gestures.

Mute has gestured [✍] (writing hand). This likely means Mute is reading the manual and wants to communicate instructions, or perhaps is asking me to describe what I see so they can look it up. Since Mute cannot speak, they are using gestures to initiate contact or signal that they have information.

Blind has gestured [🤟] (love-you / I love you / rock on / deaf sign for 'I love you' or sometimes used as a general positive/ready gesture in this context, or potentially representing the number 6 if counting fingers, but usually distinct). Given the constraints, Blind might be trying to signal readiness or a specific state. However, Blind cannot see colors. Blind can only feel. The gesture [🤟] involves thumb, index, and pinky extended. It's ambiguous without prior agreement.

My primary role is to convey visual information to those who need it.
1. **To Mute**: Mute needs to know what the bomb looks like to find the corresponding rule in the manual. Mute sees my gestures. I should spell out or use standard conventions to describe the wires and lights. Since I don't know the agreed alphabet yet, I must start with basic descriptions. The most critical info is the wire colors and the display value.
2. **To Blind**: Blind cannot see my gestures. Blind can only receive *speech*. But wait, the rules say: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." AND "You never receive speech." So, if I speak, Blind hears me. Mute also hears me? No, "Mute... Cannot Speak". But can Mute hear? The table says Mute "Cannot Speak". It doesn't explicitly say Mute cannot hear. Usually, in these puzzles, Mute can hear but not speak. Let's re-read carefully.
   - Deaf: Cannot Hear. Can See.
   - Mute: Cannot Speak. Can Read Manual. Can Gesture.
   - Blind: Cannot See. Can Touch. Can Speak? The table says "Reach the bomb... work its parts". It doesn't list "Cannot Speak" for Blind. It lists "Cannot See". So Blind CAN speak.
   
   If Blind can speak, why did Blind gesture to me? Because I am Deaf, I can't hear them. They knew I couldn't hear, so they gestured.
   
   Now, how do I get info to Blind? I must **speak**. Blind will hear my words. Mute will also hear my words (assuming Mute can hear). Or does Mute rely on gestures? The prompt says "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it." So speaking reaches both.
   
   How do I get info to Mute specifically? Mute can see gestures. Mute can also hear speech. So speech works for Mute too.
   
   The bottleneck is that I cannot hear anything. So I don't know what Mute or Blind are saying *to each other* or *to me* via voice. I only see gestures directed at me.
   
   Current State:
   - I see: Display 0, Light Orange, Wires Red/Yellow/Blue.
   - Mute gestured [✍]. This probably means "I am reading/writing" or "Give me info".
   - Blind gestured [🤟]. This is strange since Blind can speak. Maybe Blind is signaling "I'm ready" or trying to establish a code. Or maybe [🤟] stands for something specific in a pre-agreed set? We haven't agreed on anything.
   
   Strategy:
   I need to provide the visual data to the team.
   Since I can speak and gesture:
   - Speaking conveys complex text easily to Blind (who hears) and Mute (who hears).
   - Gesturing conveys symbols to Mute (who sees).
   
   I will **speak** the details of the bomb. This ensures Blind gets the color info (which they can't see but might need to verify by touch? No, Blind can't see color. But Blind needs to know *which* wire is which to cut? Or maybe the manual dictates cutting based on color. If Blind cuts blindly, they need to know which position corresponds to which color. E.g., "Wire 1 is Red").
   
   I will also **gesture** to Mute to confirm I've seen their signal and to reinforce the message visually if needed, but speech is more efficient for detailed description.
   
   Let's draft the speech content:
   "Bomb status: Display shows zero. Light is orange. There are three wires. Wire 1 is red. Wire 2 is yellow. Wire 3 is blue."
   
   This gives Blind the positional mapping (1=Red, etc.) so they can identify wires by touch if they have tactile markers, or just so they know the configuration for decision making. It gives Mute the full description to look up in the manual.
   
   Do I need to gesture? Mute saw [✍]. I should acknowledge. A simple 👍 might mean "Understood" or "OK". Or I could gesture the numbers/colors if we had a code. We don't. Speech is safer.
   
   Wait, if I speak, does Mute definitely hear? Yes, "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it."
   
   So, one clear spoken sentence covers everyone who can perceive speech.
   
   What about Blind's [🤟]? If Blind can speak, why gesture? Perhaps Blind is indicating they are listening? Or perhaps Blind is trying to say "I am blind"? Unlikely.
   
   Let's stick to transmitting the hard data first.
   
   Action:
   1. Speak the bomb configuration.
   2. Gesture 👍 to Mute to acknowledge their [✍] signal and indicate "Information provided".

   Refining the speech:
   "The display reads 0. The light is orange. The wires are: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue."

   Refining the gesture:
   To Mute: ["👍"]

```
speak(to="mute", text="The display reads 0. The light is orange. The wires are: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="The display reads 0. The light is orange. The wires are: 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb state has changed: the light is now **green** (previously orange). The display remains **0**, and wires are unchanged (1:red, 2:yellow, 3:blue).
Mute gestured [✌] (peace sign / two fingers). This likely indicates "Two" or "Option 2" or perhaps acknowledges my previous message with a specific code. Given Mute can read the manual, they might be signaling that the rule involves the number 2, or the second wire, or a condition met by "two" things.

Since I cannot hear speech, I must rely on gestures to communicate back to Mute, and speech to communicate to Blind (who hears but cannot see).
Blind needs to know the current visual state to act correctly if their action depends on color or display. Specifically, the change from Orange to Green is critical.

I will speak the updated status to Blind so they know the light is green.
I will gesture to Mute to acknowledge the update and ask for clarification on the [✌] signal if needed, or simply confirm receipt. A simple 👍 confirms "Received". Or perhaps I should gesture the colors? No standard alphabet for colors yet.
Let's assume Mute's [✌] was an instruction or confirmation. I will send the new data to Blind via speech. To Mute, I will gesture 👍 to show I saw the [✌] and am ready, or perhaps gesture ✋ (stop/wait) if I'm unsure? No, better to provide info.

Actually, looking at the flow:
Turn 1: I sent full details.
Turn 2: Light changed to Green. Mute signaled [✌].
Mute likely looked up the rule for "Display 0, Light Green" or similar in the manual. The [✌] might mean "Cut Wire 2" or "There are 2 conditions" or just "OK/Two".
Without knowing the code, I must ensure Blind knows the *current* state because Blind acts on touch. If Blind cuts Wire 2 based on Mute's hint, they need to know which one is Wire 2. I already told them "Wire 2 is yellow". That hasn't changed.
However, the light changing is a major event. Does it affect the wiring? Usually no, but it affects the *rule*.
If Mute is guiding us, they might need me to confirm the light is green. But they can't see it. Wait, Mute *can* read the manual, but does Mute see the bomb? No, only Deaf sees the bomb. So Mute relies on ME to tell them what the bomb looks like.
In Turn 1, I said "Light is orange".
Now it is "Green".
Mute might not know it changed unless I tell them.
But Mute gestured [✌]. Did they do this *after* seeing my text? They can't see my text (speech). They can see my gestures. I gestured 👍 last turn.
If Mute doesn't know the light changed, their [✌] might be based on old info (Orange).
Therefore, I MUST inform Mute that the light is now GREEN.
How to say "Green" via gesture? We don't have a code.
Maybe I should spell it out? G-R-E-E-N. Using letters as hand signs? Not provided in alphabet.
The alphabet has emojis/symbols.
Perhaps I can use a sequence?
Or maybe I should just speak to Blind and hope Mute infers? No, Mute is key for rules.
Is there a way to indicate "Change"?
Maybe I gesture ✋ (Stop/Wait) then point?
Let's look at the symbols again.
👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 ...
Maybe [☝] means One, [✌] means Two...
If I want to convey "Green", maybe I can't directly.
But wait, if I speak, Mute receives it?
Rule: "When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it."
YES! Mute CAN HEAR. Mute just CANNOT SPEAK.
So I can just SAY "The light is now green" and Mute will hear it.
This simplifies everything. I don't need complex gestures for information transfer if speech reaches both.

Plan:
1. Speak the new status: "Update: The light is now green. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue."
2. Gesture to Mute to acknowledge their [✌] and ask for next step? Or just wait for them to process the audio.
   Since Mute heard the update, they can re-evaluate the manual.
   I will gesture 👍 to Mute to say "Message sent/Understood your signal".

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: The light is now green. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: The light is now green. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed again, from green to **red**. The display remains 0 and the wires are unchanged.
In the previous turn, I spoke the status update ("light is now green") which reached both Mute and Blind. Since there were no new gestures or actions from them in response to that specific update (or rather, the board just updated), it implies they might be waiting for a stable state or processing the rule change.

However, the most critical piece of information is the current visual state. The light is now Red. This matches Wire 1's color. Often in these puzzles, "Red Light" + "Red Wire" triggers a specific rule (e.g., cut the matching wire, or don't touch the matching wire).

I must immediately inform Mute and Blind of this change so they can consult the manual or act accordingly.
Speech reaches both Mute and Blind.
Gestures reach only Mute.

I will speak the new status clearly.
I will also gesture to Mute to ensure they notice the update if they weren't paying close attention to audio, perhaps using a symbol that indicates "Change" or "Alert". There isn't a standard "alert" symbol, but pointing 👉 or raising hand ✋ might draw attention. Or simply repeating the confirmation 👍 after stating the fact? No, better to use a distinct signal if possible. But without a pre-agreed code, speech is the primary channel for data.

Let's stick to clear speech.
"The light is now red."

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: The light is now red. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: The light is now red. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed back to **orange**. The display remains 0 and the wires are unchanged.
Since there were no new gestures or speech from Mute or Blind in response to the previous updates (Red, then Green), it suggests they might be waiting for a specific condition or perhaps the manual dictates an action based on a sequence or a stable state. However, the rapid cycling of colors (Orange -> Green -> Red -> Orange) without any input from them is concerning. It implies either:
1. They haven't acted yet because they don't know what to do.
2. The bomb is changing states automatically and we need to wait for a specific color that matches a rule.

Given that I am Deaf, I cannot hear if they are discussing this among themselves. I only see their gestures directed at me. Since they sent nothing last turn, they might be confused or waiting for *me* to signal something other than just "status update".

However, my primary constraint is that I cannot touch the bomb. I must rely on them.
If the light is Orange again, and Wire 1 is Red, Wire 2 Yellow, Wire 3 Blue... none match the light color directly (except maybe if Orange matched a wire, but it doesn't).

Let's assume the standard logic: The manual likely says "Cut wire X if Light is Y".
Mute reads the manual. Blind touches the wires.
I provide the visual data.

Since I've already spoken the full details multiple times, repeating the exact same sentence might not add value unless I emphasize the change. But the most useful thing now might be to ask Mute for confirmation or instruction via gesture, since they can read the manual and might have found the rule for "Display 0, Light Orange".

In Turn 1, Mute gestured [✍] (Writing/Reading).
In Turn 2, Mute gestured [✌] (Two).
In Turn 3, No gesture.
In Turn 4, No gesture.

Maybe [✌] meant "Wait" or "Two options"? Or maybe it was related to the green light?
If the light is Orange now, and Mute hasn't reacted, maybe they are still processing.

I will send the status update again to ensure they know it reverted to Orange. This is crucial because if they acted on Red/Green instructions, those are now invalid.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Update: The light is now orange. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: The light is now orange. Display is still 0. Wires are 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👆"]) 
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[yellow] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The light has changed to **green** again. Mute has gestured [✌] (Two) once more, specifically when the light is green.

This repetition of the gesture [✌] during a "Green" state strongly suggests that Mute is trying to communicate a specific instruction or rule related to the number 2 or the second wire when the light is green. Since I cannot hear speech from them, and they are repeating this signal in response to my updates, it is highly likely that the manual says something like "If Light is Green, Cut Wire 2".

I need to confirm this hypothesis with Blind, who can actually touch and cut the wires. Blind hears me.
I should explicitly tell Blind: "Mute signals 'Two' when light is Green. This likely means Cut Wire 2."
Wire 2 is Yellow.

So, the action for Blind would be to cut the Yellow wire.

I will speak this interpretation clearly to both Mute (to confirm I understand their gesture) and Blind (to give the command).

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see you signaling Two for Green. Interpreting as: Cut Wire 2.")
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals 'Two' when light is Green. Please cut Wire 2 (the yellow one).")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```
